stem: A random variable X takes values 1, 2, or 3 with probabilities proportional to its value. That is, P(X = x) = x/c for x = 1, 2, 3 and some constant c. What is P(X = 2)?

per_option_rationale.rationale: 2/3 arises from setting c=3 (the maximum value) instead of c=6 (the sum of values), giving P(X=2) = 2/3.
1/6 = P(X=1) = 1/c with c=6; the student reads P(X=1) instead of P(X=2).
1/2 arises from treating probabilities as equal (1/3 each) and then incorrectly summing P(X=1)+P(X=2)=2/6 and misidentifying the result as 1/2.

explanation: The probabilities P(X=1)=1/c, P(X=2)=2/c, P(X=3)=3/c must sum to 1: (1+2+3)/c = 6/c = 1, so c = 6. Hence P(X=2) = 2/6 = 1/3.

explanation_sections.punchline: Find c by imposing sum = 1: c = 1+2+3 = 6, then P(X=2) = 2/6 = 1/3.
explanation_sections.approach: Identify model: PMF proportional to x. Decisive move: use sum rule to find the normalizing constant c. Sum all probabilities: sum(x/c for x in {1,2,3}) = 6/c = 1 => c = 6. Then substitute: P(X=2) = 2/6 = 1/3.
explanation_sections.lesson: When a PMF is proportional to some expression, always find the normalizing constant by setting the total to 1.
explanation_sections.timing: 50 seconds. Sum 1+2+3=6, so c=6. P(X=2)=2/6=1/3. Trap: using c=3 (the number of values) instead of c=6 (sum of values).
